How to Write a Teacher Resume

A teacher resume should show subject and grade expertise, learning outcomes, classroom practice, and contribution to the school community. Use student evidence carefully and never expose private information.

Example

Teacher resume summary

Use this as a pattern for level, scope, specialty, and evidence. Do not copy facts that are not yours.

Middle school teacher with 7 years of experience in literacy instruction, assessment, and differentiated learning. Improved grade-level reading proficiency by 18 percentage points and led a team-wide intervention plan.
Recommended order

How to structure the resume

  1. Contact details and target title. Use the normal title from the job posting and provide working contact links.
  2. Focused summary. Establish your level, setting, specialty, and one representative outcome.
  3. Recent relevant experience. Use reverse chronological order and give the most space to work that resembles the target role.
  4. Role-specific skills. Keep a scannable list, then prove the important skills in bullets.
  5. Education and credentials. State your active teaching license, endorsements, subjects, and jurisdictions clearly. Put student teaching and practicum experience in the work section when applying for a first role.
Use only what you can support

Skills to include

Match the employer's terminology when it accurately describes your experience.

  • Curriculum planning
  • Classroom management
  • Assessment
  • Differentiated instruction
  • Family communication
  • Learning technology
  • Student support
  • Team leadership
Evidence ideas

Useful metrics for a teacher resume

Numbers should clarify scope or change. They do not need to be revenue figures.

Learning

Growth, proficiency, or completion rates

Reach

Students, classes, or programs served

Contribution

Curriculum, mentoring, clubs, or team leadership

Writing patterns

Teacher resume bullet examples

Adapt the action, context, and result to your own verified work.

  • Improved grade-level reading proficiency by 18 percentage points.
  • Designed differentiated lessons for a class of thirty-two learners.
  • Led a teaching team that aligned assessment and intervention plans.
  • Introduced weekly family updates and increased conference participation by 22%.
Look for

Strong signals

  • Instructional practice
  • Student growth
  • Classroom culture
  • Community contribution
Avoid

Common mistakes

  • Listing duties every teacher performs
  • Using student data without context or privacy
  • Omitting grade, subject, or curriculum
  • A skills section made only of personality traits

Questions, answered

Resume FAQ

What should a teacher resume include?

Lead with instructional practice, show relevant curriculum planning experience in context, and use achievement bullets that explain scope and outcome.

What skills belong on a teacher resume?

Prioritize skills from the target job that you can prove in experience, projects, education, or credentials. Useful examples include curriculum planning, classroom management, assessment, differentiated instruction.

Can I use the example numbers and bullet points?

No. The examples demonstrate structure and specificity. Replace every action, number, tool, and result with evidence that is true for your own work.

Which resume format should I use?

Reverse chronological format works for most candidates. Use a combination format when projects or transferable skills need more emphasis, but keep dates and work history clear.
